findings.explanation: HOL4's only clause is locnrow (POSN r c) = r. The definition goes through Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition (Defn.sml:1192), i.e. new_specification of exactly that clause (Prim_rec.sml:281). No ARB completion is made, so the values at UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are open and may differ. Lean sends both to the same ARB : Nat. It therefore proves locnrow UNKNOWNpt = locnrow EOFpt by rfl, and also locnrow UNKNOWNpt = ARB and locnrow UNKNOWNpt = locncol UNKNOWNpt. The saved HOL4 theorems decide none of these.
findings.repair:
opaque locnrow_unspec : locn → Nat

noncomputable def locnrow : locn → Nat
  | .POSN r _ => r
  | l => locnrow_unspec l
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location
open CmlTS

example : locnrow locn.UNKNOWNpt = locnrow locn.EOFpt := rfl
findings.hol4_check: ?h. (!r c. h (POSN r c) = r) /\ h UNKNOWNpt <> h EOFpt

findings.explanation: HOL4 specifies only locn_rowupdate f (POSN r c) = POSN (f r) c, by new_specification through Prim_rec. The results on UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are open and may depend on f and on the constructor. Lean maps both to the one value ARB : locn for every f. It therefore proves locn_rowupdate f UNKNOWNpt = locn_rowupdate g EOFpt for all f and g, by rfl. The saved HOL4 theorems leave this equation open.
findings.repair:
opaque locn_rowupdate_unspec : (Nat → Nat) → locn → locn

noncomputable def locn_rowupdate (f : Nat → Nat) : locn → locn
  | .POSN r c => .POSN (f r) c
  | l => locn_rowupdate_unspec f l
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location
open CmlTS

example (f g : Nat → Nat) : locn_rowupdate f locn.UNKNOWNpt = locn_rowupdate g locn.EOFpt := rfl
findings.hol4_check: ?h. (!f r c. h f (POSN r c) = POSN (f r) c) /\ h I UNKNOWNpt <> h I EOFpt
